content.title: About
content.content: Pumpkin pie is a dessert made from pumpkin purée, eggs, sugar, spices (cinnamon, ginger, cloves) and a crust. The pumpkin gives it a characteristic orange color, a smooth flavor and aroma, while the spices add warmth and depth.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpkin was introduced to Europe from North America in the 16th century.
Pumpkin pie became a traditional dish in the United States for Thanksgiving.
There are more than 30 pumpkin varieties, but “Hokkaido” or “Sugar” pumpkins are most commonly used for pies.
Pumpkin is rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A.
In some countries pumpkin pie is served with whipped cream or ice cream.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is a powerful antioxidant and a precursor of vitamin A, supporting vision and immunity.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with many desserts, pumpkin pie contains relatively little saturated fat.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: Provides vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immune defense and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Pumpkin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pumpkin or to ingredients in the filling.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Pumpkin pie often contains a high amount of sugar, which can be problematic for people with diabetes.

items.title: Calorie-dense servings
items.content: Large portions can lead to excess calorie intake.

items.title: Egg content
items.content: People allergic to eggs should choose egg‑free versions or use suitable substitutes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pumpkin pie is served warm or at room temperature, commonly topped with whipped cream, ice cream, or a nut crumble. Slice into portions and keep refrigerated for a few days.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the finished pumpkin pie in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze individual slices in a freezer‑safe bag – they retain quality for up to 2 months.
